```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-dev
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/iam.yaml`
```yaml

apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: User
metadata:
  name: myapp-dev
spec:
  userName: myapp-dev
  # Attach both the existing policy and the new logs policy (or use inlinePolicies below)

---
# Existing policy with logs bucket access added
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-dev-policy
spec:
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-dev/*"
        },
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
spec:
  bucketName: myapp-logs-prod
  versioningConfiguration:
    status: Enabled
  serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
        sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlockConfiguration:
    blockPublicAcls: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicAcls: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/iam.yaml`
```yaml
# Existing prod Role, unchanged reference below
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
spec:
  roleName: myapp-prod
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/THUMBPRINT"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "oidc.eks.REGION.amazonaws.com/id/THUMBPRINT:sub": "system:serviceaccount:default:myapp"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }

---
# Existing policy with logs bucket access added
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod-policy
spec:
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-assets-prod/*"
        },
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

---

**Integration notes:**

- The `iam.yaml` manifests above show the updated Policy documents with logs bucket access separated into a distinct statement for clarity. Both the assets and logs buckets are now grantees of GetObject/PutObject, but only on their respective resources (no cross-bucket access).
- If your existing setup uses `inlinePolicies` on the User/Role directly rather than separate Policy resources, move the policy document into an inline policy block on the User or Role spec.
- Ensure the Policy resources are attached to their respective User (dev) and Role (prod) via the principal's `attachedPolicies` field or equivalent, if not already implicit via naming convention.
- Both bucket manifests enable versioning, AES256 encryption, and block all public access as required.
